news.headline: Trump rejects Iran's Strait of Hormuz proposal; Brent crude jumps to $105.64/bbl (+1.39%)
news.what_happened: US President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sustaining Middle East tensions and pushing Brent crude above $105 per barrel in early Asian trading.
news.why_it_matters: India imports ~85% of its crude oil needs. Rising crude widens the current account deficit, pressures the rupee, and raises input costs across airlines, paints, tyres, chemicals and FMCG. However, upstream producers like ONGC and OIL benefit directly from higher realizations.

news.headline: US 10-Year Treasury Yield surges to 5.184% — a 20-year high
news.what_happened: US 10Y bond yield rose to 5.184%, its highest level in 20 years, as strong US economic data and persistent inflation keep the Fed in hawkish mode. US equity futures fell 0.3% in early Asian trade.
news.why_it_matters: FIIs have sold Rs 17,131 Cr in Indian equities in September alone, with Rs 3,694 Cr on Friday. Rising US yields make risk-free US assets more attractive, sustaining FII outflows. Nifty is on its 7th consecutive losing week. Rate-sensitive sectors face dual headwinds.

news.headline: Bank strike AVERTED — UFBU defers 3-day strike after late-night IBA agreement
news.what_happened: The United Forum of Bank Unions deferred its September 28-30 nationwide bank strike after reaching an agreement with the Indian Banks' Association. Banks are fully operational today including clearing houses and corporate banking.
news.why_it_matters: Removes near-term disruption risk for banking sector. Positive catalyst for bank stocks that had been pricing in operational risk. India's liquidity surplus at Rs 11.6 lakh crore (3% of GDP) further supports domestic banking environment.

news.headline: China industrial profits at weakest pace this year — +4.2% in August YoY
news.what_happened: China's industrial profits grew just 4.2% YoY in August, the slowest pace in 2026, as consumer demand weakness persists and energy costs rise. Shanghai Composite down 1.1%, South Korea Kospi down 2% this morning.
news.why_it_matters: China is the world's largest consumer of steel, aluminum and copper. Weak industrial data signals soft demand for metals. Indian metal producers face pricing headwinds. Risk-off sentiment from Asia adds to FII selling pressure on Nifty.

news.headline: Natural Gas falls 3.35% to $3.117/MMBtu — multi-week low
news.what_happened: Natural gas futures dropped 3.35% to $3.117/MMBtu on mild weather forecasts and higher-than-expected US storage builds.
news.why_it_matters: Natural gas is the primary feedstock (60-70% of variable cost) for urea, ammonia and DAP fertilizer production. A sustained gas price decline directly expands margins for DEEPAKFERT, GNFC and COROMANDEL — one of the few cost tailwinds in today's otherwise bearish market.

picks.catalyst: Brent crude surges to $105.64/bbl (+1.39%) on Iran/Strait of Hormuz tensions
picks.logic: ONGC is India's largest upstream oil producer. Every dollar rise in Brent directly increases per-barrel realization. At $105 Brent, ONGC upstream margins expand meaningfully. Unlike most Indian sectors that suffer from rising crude, ONGC directly benefits. In today's risk-off market, it is one of the few domestic sectors with a genuine P&L tailwind from overnight news. Geopolitical risk sustaining crude keeps the thesis alive intraday.

picks.logic: Deepak Fertilisers produces urea, ammonia and TAN using natural gas as primary feedstock, accounting for ~60-65% of variable production cost. A 3.35% gas price decline on a single day translates directly to margin expansion. Unlike most sectors facing headwinds today, fertilizer companies are cost beneficiaries. Stock near flat from previous close Rs 1,361.40, offering clean entry for a gas-cost tailwind play with limited macro overhang.
